page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-24 is a compute-focused instance powered by 5th Gen Intel Xeon Emerald Rapids processors (custom Xeon 8581C). Built on the x86_64 architecture, the virtual machine provides 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. Memory allocation is configured at 48 GB of RAM, resulting in a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core). The CPU features 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX-TILE, AMX-INT8). The instance does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, requiring reliance on external network-attached block storage.

Benchmark results highlight solid computational throughput and instruction-level vector performance. In Geekbench testing, the server achieved a single-core score of 1986.0 (top 25%) alongside an image processing result of 14131.0. Intel AMX hardware acceleration and vector extensions demonstrate strong efficiency in lightweight inference tasks, delivering 433.41 tokens per second on text generation using a small 135M language model, placing it in the top 10% of tested instances. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 31.82 GB/sec. Across standard workloads, multi-core metrics remain steady, recording a PassMark CPU score of 34445.22, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression of 148.45 GB/sec, and memory bandwidth of 140.86 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads.

The 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio makes the instance cost-efficient for CPU-intensive processes where memory consumption is low to moderate. Because local disks and hardware accelerators are absent, workloads that require massive datasets residing strictly in local non-volatile storage will need auxiliary storage configurations. The instance is suited for batch processing, CI/CD pipelines, compilation tasks, lightweight matrix operations, web serving clusters, and CPU-based machine learning inference.

It provides 24 dedicated vCPUs over 12 physical cores at 2.3 GHz, 260 MB of L3 cache, and 48 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio. Equipped with AVX-512 and Intel AMX extensions, it delivers notable single-core throughput, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 1986.0, alongside 433.41 tokens per second for small-model LLM generation. The instance has no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external block storage for data persistence. With balanced compute density and moderate memory per thread, c4-highcpu-24 is suited for continuous integration, code compilation, lightweight matrix computation, web serving, and CPU-driven batch processing.
